chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from al-Ḥārith al-Naṣrī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: “The salat (prayer) of the day is sixteen rakʿahs: eight when the sun declines, and eight after al-ẓuhr, and four rakʿahs after al-maghrib. O Ḥārith, do not leave them in travel or in residence. And two rakʿahs after al-ʿishāʾ—my father used to perform them while seated, and I perform them while standing. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform thirteen rakʿahs of the night.”

key_terms.ثَلَاثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً مِنَ اللَّيْلِ: thirteen rakʿahs performed during the night
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, marking the start of the noon period

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about the recommended daily and nightly nawāfil prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the recommended daily and nightly supererogatory salat (prayer), specifying their number and times. It also emphasizes maintaining certain prayers both in travel and residence, and it references the practice of the Imam’s father and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding night worship.
